rationale: The board's question is whether switching on feedback causes better hand hygiene, and the 16 wards can be randomised because the intervention is a software switch. A cluster randomised trial with pairs of wards that share float staff randomised together limits contamination (c5); the primary outcome is direct observation by external observers, equally visible on both arms, because the system's own figure can be gamed (c3) and visible observation inflates compliance (c2). The retrieved trial (c1) suggests an effect large enough to be worth testing. Reporting follows the CONSORT extension for cluster trials.
alternatives: Before-after comparison on all wards (refused: cannot separate feedback from observation effects and secular change)
Stepped-wedge rollout (refused: six months is too short for several steps and the board needs a parallel comparison)
Decision based on the badge figure alone (refused: the measure the intervention acts on)
guidelines: CONSORT extension for cluster randomised trials
whyNotMoreComplex: A trial with infection outcomes would need many hospitals and years; the observed-compliance trial answers the purchasing question within the window.

decision.statement: Prepare a cluster randomised trial of real-time badge feedback on 16 wards randomised in pairs that share float staff, with directly observed compliance by external observers as the primary outcome, for submission to the ethics board before January 2027.
decision.question: Should the hospital test real-time badge feedback in a ward-randomised trial before buying the licence for all wards?

criteria.text: A randomised comparison has reported an effect of feedback large enough to be worth testing locally.
An outcome independent of the feedback system is available and can be made equally visible in both arms.
The board buys the licence for all wards before the trial reports.

gates.requirement: Infection prevention committee endorsement of a ward-randomised comparison
gates.evidence: Minute IPC-2026-22 dated 2026-09-15, supplied by the investigator

gates.requirement: Staff council agreement allowing ward-level evaluation use of badge data
gates.evidence: Agreement JSC-2026-07, supplied by the investigator

alternatives: Buy the licence and monitor the badge figure
decision.note: Rests on ledger claims c1 to c3 from retrieved records; both gates are met on investigator-supplied records, so trial preparation can start.

summary: Cluster randomised trial of paired wards recommended; the decision rests on three ledger claims and both gates are met.
